extracted.intended_audience: experimental natural philosophers / scientists (readers of Philosophical Transactions, 17th-century experimentalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, conducting, and reporting pneumatical/vacuum experiments on animals and substances, including controls, apparatus sealing, timing, and careful phenomenological description. Emphasis on reproducible procedure and separating observation from speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermetic sealing to isolate included air
rubrics_metrics.description: The upper part of the long neck of the glass was... hermetically sealed by the help of a lamp and a pair of bellows, that we might be sure that the imprisoned animal should breathe no other air than that which filled the receiver at the time when it was nipped up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the vessel is hermetically sealed so the subject breathes only the enclosed air; seal method (lamp, nipping) should be documented. This prevents exchange with external atmosphere and isolates the variable of included air composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor pressure/degree of exhaustion with a gauge
rubrics_metrics.description: I cast my eyes upon the gauge, wherein I could not perceive any sensible change of the mercury's station.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a sensitive gauge to record the degree of air removal; report whether the gauge shows sensible change. Note that lack of a visible gauge change does not necessarily preclude physiological effect, so report gauge readings (or absence of change) alongside observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test reversibility by admitting fresh air (revival check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Being unwilling to give over the mouse without trying what fresh air would do to recover him, I caused the sealed part of the glass to be broken off... I obtained after a while some faint tokens of life; ... fresh air was frequently blown in by a pair of bellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging death vs. stupor, admit fresh air (in a controlled manner, e.g., via bellows or breaking the seal) and observe for revival. Record timing and method of air admission and any recovery signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for temperature vs. air composition effects
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy some curious persons, that it is not want of coldness, but something else in the included air, that makes it destroy the birds... we made the following experiment... the phial with the sick bird was immersed [in water with sal ammoniac made exceedingly cold]... it did not appear... that the great refrigeration... did sensibly revive or refresh the drooping animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include controls that isolate temperature effects from air-composition effects (e.g., extreme refrigeration) and report negative/positive results. Describe the cooling procedure and duration precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for vessel volume relative to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: By reason of the largeness of the vessel in comparison of so small an animal, he seemed... rather drooping than very near death...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report vessel size/volume and consider its relation to subject size; larger volume may delay deleterious effects. Include this factor when comparing outcomes across trials or species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure receiver against unpermitted return of air
rubrics_metrics.description: We withdrew, but not solicitously, the air, and secured the vessel against the unpermitted return of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and verify measures taken to prevent ingress of external air during storage/observation (stoppers, cuffs, clamps). Note any checks performed to confirm continued exhaustion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate controls (non-exhausted comparative receivers)
rubrics_metrics.description: We put them into like receivers, and in one of them shut up the caterpillars together with the air, which from the other was exhausted. The event was... the one which had the air... continued to move... whereas that glass whence the air had been drawn out... showed... no motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run parallel control receivers left with normal air to compare behavior. Report side-by-side outcomes to attribute effects to vacuum rather than handling or enclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise timings and durations
rubrics_metrics.description: The bird in about half an hour appeared to be sick and drooping, and the faintness and difficulty of breathing increased for about two hours and a half... the animal died within a minute or two of a just hour... kept him there about 48 hours...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exact or approximate time points for onset of symptoms, duration until death or revival, and intervals between observations. Many phenomena (revival after hours/days) depend on time, so log timings carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time for delayed recovery before declaring death
rubrics_metrics.description: Though they continued to appear so, till I went to bed; yet I thought fit to try, whether time might not at length recover them, and leaving them all night in the receiver, I found the next day, that three if not four of them were perfectly alive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume immediate death if no motion is observed; allow sufficient time and repeated checks (overnight, days) before concluding irreversible death. Document repeated checks and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use magnification/microscopy for very small organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: By the help of a double convex glass (that was so set in a frame as to serve me as a microscope on such occasions) I was not able to see any of them stir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mites and other tiny organisms, employ suitable magnification. Describe the optical aids used and how they influence detectability of motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for contaminants/artifacts from apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: They were very lively just before they were sealed up... yet they grew almost motionless as soon as the air was exhausted; though I then suspected... that they were much inconvenienced by some small glutinous substance that seemed to have got into the small receiver from the vapours of the cement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify, avoid, and report possible contaminants (cements, fumes, residues) that might affect subjects. If suspected, note how contamination was detected and mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe qualitative phenomenology in detail
rubrics_metrics.description: He appeared to be very ill at ease, and seemed to sweat out of the abdomen many little drops of liquor... the inward parts of their bodies seemed to be almost vanished... there emerged from divers parts of her body store of bubbles...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rich descriptive details: convulsions, secretions, tumidity, bubbles, color changes, smells, fumes. These qualitative notes are essential for interpreting mechanisms and for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document procedural variations and apparatus manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: By frequently inverting the receiver (which I took care should be pretty long to let them fall from one extreme to the other,) they would fall like dead animals without displaying their wings...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record any manipulations (inversion, placement in sun, proximity to fire, how opened) that may affect results. Small handling differences can change outcomes; note them explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare substances' volatility and air-dependent phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: If the phial be unstopped, so that the external air be permitted to come in, and touch the surface of the liquor, within a quarter of a minute or less, there will... be elevated a copious white smoke... One may compare with this liquor another smoking one... the fumes that proceed from it may fright many from daring to meddle with it: whereas this our red spirit has been found potently medicinal...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with volatile or 'smoking' liquids, report how contact with air affects them (fumes, smell, visibility) and compare with known substances. Note safety/handling concerns and any medicinal or corrosive properties observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple species/sizes and varied subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Such an experiment as the former we made with like success upon a small bird... we made trial upon ordinary white snails... whether efts and leeches might not yet be more able to continue in our vacuum than a snail... we inclosed divers of them, especially that I might see, whether... some or other of them, by the help of their large wings, would be able to fly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test across species, sizes, and life-forms to generalize findings. Report all subject types, sizes, and relevant anatomical features (wings, shells) that may influence results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify exhaustion and check receiver integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: By opening the receiver at length under water, we perceived that about half the air had been drawn out... I was satisfied the receiver was immediately before as well exhausted as others are wont to be in our pneumatical experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include procedures to verify how well-exhausted a receiver is and to test seals (e.g., opening under water, observing ingress of liquid). Report such verification steps and findings to establish experiment validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep observation separate from speculative interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: My purpose in this tract, to forbear sidings in controversies, keeps me from taking notice of the speculations suggested by some of the phaenomena of this liquor; which yet I thought I might lawfully mention, as far as I have done it, because it but adventures upon giving one of the uses rather of the air, than immediately of respiration itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish observed facts from speculative explanations. Present observations clearly and avoid overreaching theoretical claims within the experimental report; note when speculation is being offered.
